Application Materials.content:
Required application materials include:
- **A degree transcript** in one of the suggested disciplines.
- **One reference**.
- **A personal statement**.
- Overseas applicants should also supply evidence of their English language ability, usually via an IELTS test. Other acceptable tests by UCL can be found on [UCL’s English Language requirements webpage](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/english-language-requirements).
For the personal statement, UCL asks applicants to address:
- Why do you want to study Business Analytics at a postgraduate level;
- What particularly attracts you to this programme and to the UCL School of Management;
- How does your academic and professional background meet the demands of this challenging programme;
- What your post-degree aspirations are and how does your success on this programme support them?
The personal statement is an opportunity to illustrate whether your reasons for applying to this programme match what the programme will deliver and is a right fit for you. Applicants should use this part of the application to show uniqueness, critical thinking, personality, academic prowess, and passion for business, technology, and data.

Interview Requirements.content: If you meet the entry requirements and are suitable for the MSc Business Analytics programme, you may be invited for an online interview. Those invited to interview will have a window of **7 calendar days** from receipt of the email to complete the interview. Failure to complete the interview within this window will lead to an unsuccessful application.

Application Deadlines.content:
**Start date:** September 2026
**Application deadline:** Open on **20th October 2025** and close on **26th June 2026 at 5pm UK time** for applicants who require a visa; and on **28th August 2026** for those who do not.
A staged admissions process is in place for this programme:
- Applications submitted, and considered complete by **8 December 2025** can expect to receive a response by **9 February 2026**.
- Applications submitted, and considered complete by **20 February 2026** can expect to receive a response by **24 April 2026**.
- Applications submitted, and considered complete by **17 April 2026** can expect to receive a response by **5 June 2026**.
- Applications submitted, and considered complete after **17 April 2026** that require a visa can expect to receive a response by end of **August 2026**; and those who do not require a visa can expect to receive a response by **18 September 2026**.
Full-time course dates: **Mid-September 2026 - Mid-September 2027**.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **Entry:** Minimum of **2:1 honours or equivalent in a relevant discipline**.
- **Academic Profile:** The minimum entrance requirements are an **upper second-class (2:1) Bachelor’s degree from a UK university or an overseas equivalent** and a **strong aptitude for quantitative analysis**. Applicants are likely to have studied a range of degrees including **business, engineering, computer science, economics, and psychology**. International students may ascertain qualification equivalents from the [UCL international students website](http://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/international-students).
- **Contextual offers:** UCL normally requires an upper second-class Bachelor’s degree from a UK university or an overseas qualification of an equivalent standard. Applicants with **lower second-class degrees (UK 2:2 or the overseas equivalent)** may be considered if their application is supported strongly by relevant experience.
- Technical skills: UCL recommends applicants have experience of using a programming language, as this will be required throughout the programme.
- Mathematical/statistical skills: A good mathematical understanding is needed for the programme.
- If degree results are just under a 2:1, applicants who fall short of the academic requirements by a small margin but have **significant work experience (over 2 years) in relevant fields** may be considered on an exceptional case basis; this is not guaranteed to secure a place.
- **China-specific equivalency:** A **four-year bachelor’s degree from a recognised Chinese higher education institution** will be considered. The required grade varies depending on the awarding university.
- **China-specific 2:1 equivalent:** Applicants from UCL’s list of Chinese universities, which includes a selection of Project 211, Project 985, and Double First-Class universities, need a Bachelor’s degree with a **minimum weighted average mark of 85%** for upper second-class (2:1). Not all universities from these projects are included.
- **China-specific 2:1 equivalent for all other recognised Chinese universities:** Applicants from all other universities recognised by the Chinese Ministry of Education need a Bachelor’s degree with a **minimum weighted average mark of 90%** for upper second-class (2:1).

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Business Analytics MSc requires UCL English language **Level 2**. Applicants whose first language is not English must provide evidence that their spoken and written English is adequate. UCL’s preferred English language qualification is IELTS.
- **IELTS Academic:** **overall 7.0**, with **minimum 6.5 in each component/subtest**. IELTS Academic Online is accepted. IELTS One Skill Retake is not accepted.
- **TOEFL iBT, tests taken from 21 January 2026:** **overall 4.5**, with **4.5 in reading, writing, speaking and listening**.
- **TOEFL iBT, tests taken before 21 January 2026:** **overall 96**, with **24/30 in reading and writing** and **22/30 in speaking and listening**. Tests must be within the two-year timeframe. TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition is accepted; TOEFL iBT MyBestScore is not acceptable. UCL’s institution code for TOEFL is **9163**.
- **Cambridge English C2 Proficiency (CPE):** **overall 180**, with **172 in all subtests**.
- **Cambridge English C1 Advanced (CAE):** **overall 180**, with **172 in all subtests**.
- **Pearson Test of English (Academic) / PTE Academic:** **overall 76**, with **minimum 75 in each Communicative Skill**.
Any student who is not a national of a UK Home Office majority English-speaking country is required to provide recent evidence of English language proficiency. Those who have studied in English or completed at least **12 months** of academic education leading to an awarded qualification in a country UCL considers to be “majority English-speaking” may not be required to provide further English Language qualification/test results. More information is available on UCL’s [English Language Requirements](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/english-language-requirements) page.

Program Overview.content:
**Start date:** September 2026
**Duration:** 12 months full-time
**Location:** This programme is delivered in person at UCL School of Management’s Canary Wharf campus. The majority of classes are taught at [Levels 38, 49, and 50 of One Canada Square, Canary Wharf](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/about/canary-wharf), UCL’s home within London’s global business district. Some optional modules will take place at the Bloomsbury campus, which will also be open to students. The course lasts for a full calendar year from mid-September 2026 to mid-September 2027 and is not offered part-time.
Join this one-year MSc in Business Analytics at the UCL School of Management to prepare for data analytics and leadership roles by developing the skills needed to unlock the value of data and understand how it is revolutionising areas such as strategy, marketing, and operations. The programme develops understanding of the nuances, potential, and limitations of data, as well as statistical and computational skills to make effective use of the latest analytics tools and methods, frame complex data-driven business problems, analyse data with appropriate statistical techniques, and communicate analytics results to senior leadership, business partners, and customers.
The UCL Business Analytics programme provides a rigorous, practical foundation and a platform for careers with global companies and high-growth businesses tackling world-scale problems, with opportunities to tap into partnerships to grow networks and skills further.
On UCL’s Business Analytics MSc programme, students develop a rigorous understanding of how companies use data to make decisions and improve business performance. The programme combines modules exploring how data and analytics are transforming key areas of business, such as decision-making, strategy, marketing, and operations, with modules providing the statistical and computational foundations needed to use the latest business analytics tools and platforms. During the year, students undertake six core modules, two optional modules, and complete a Consulting Project/Dissertation. Students gain experience in data analysis techniques including computational thinking, validation and testing models, manipulating datasets, regression models, and statistical modelling, with many modules requiring leading business analytics tools such as Python.
The programme is delivered through lectures, optional workshops, and project work. Assessment methods include in-person examinations, tests, quizzes, individual coursework, group coursework, presentations, and a dissertation project. Students typically study four modules in Term One and four modules in Term Two, of which two are selected from the optional module list. In Term Three, students undertake the supervised dissertation project.
In Term Three, students may undertake either a practical consulting project with organisations that have provided a challenging analytical project, or an independent consulting/research project. Projects require the application of skills learned in Terms One and Two and have historically required students to work with leading-edge tools and techniques, resulting in a dissertation report of 12,000 words and a 15-minute presentation. Dissertation project types include research projects, technical projects, and consultative projects.
The teaching team brings together people with experience of how companies are evolving their management practices in a complex, interconnected and data-driven world and how they are employing the latest business analytics platforms and tools to make decisions and improve business performance. Dimitris Giraleas is Programme Director. The core teaching team includes [Alastair Moore](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/people/alastairmoore), Assistant Professor; [Anil Doshi](http://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/people/anildoshi), Assistant Professor; [Zhenyu Zhang](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/people/mengzhenyuzhang), Assistant Professor; [Tjun Hoh](http://management.ucl.ac.uk/people/tjunyeehoh), Assistant Professor; and [Wei Miao](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/people/miaowei), Assistant Professor.
UCL School of Management is AACSB accredited, a global mark of excellence recognising its commitment to innovative, research-led teaching, rigorous academic standards, and preparing students for impactful global careers in business and management. Students also benefit from extensive industry networks and close links with many global companies and high-growth businesses.
The Careers service offered to MSc Business Analytics students is designed to help build a strong foundation for early career success through tailored support, employer engagement, and alumni connections. MSc Business Analytics students receive bespoke careers support from a specialist careers team, including one-to-one career coaching with professionally-certified, industry-focused Careers Consultants, access to a global alumni network, online resources, and a Careers and Professional Development Programme for postgraduate taught students.
Graduates pursue global careers across a wide range of roles, sectors, and geographies. Popular sectors include consulting, banking and finance, marketing, technology, and data and analytics. Top job titles among recent graduates include Data analysts, Programmers and software development professionals, Actuaries, economists and statisticians, Information technology professionals, IT business analysts, architects and systems designers. Top companies graduates have secured roles in include Bloomberg LP, 173 Tech, Burberry Ltd, CenterPoint, Cloud IQ and EY.

Curriculum.content:
- **Start date:** September 2026. **Duration:** 12 months full-time. **Location:** This programme is delivered in person at UCL’s Canary Wharf campus. Full-time course dates: Mid-September 2026 - Mid-September 2027. The programme is not offered as part-time study.
- During the year, students undertake six core modules, two optional modules, and complete a Consulting Project/Dissertation. Students typically study four modules in Term One and four modules in Term Two, of which two are selected from the optional module list. In Term Three, students undertake the supervised dissertation project.
- The programme is delivered through a combination of lectures, optional workshops and project work. Assessment methods include in-person examinations, tests, quizzes, individual coursework, group coursework, presentations and a dissertation project. Each taught module is delivered over 10 weeks, with three contact hours per week comprising lecture content and interactive components; some modules may have additional workshop sessions. Students should spend approximately 7-12 hours a week for each module on assessment and independent study.
- Term One core modules: [**MSIN0093 Business Strategy and Analytics**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/business-strategy-and-analytics/MSIN0093); [**MSIN0094 Marketing Analytics**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/marketing-analytics/MSIN0094); [**MSIN0096 Statistical Foundations for Business Analytics**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/mathematical-foundations-of-business-analytics/MSIN0096); [**MSIN0143 Programming for Business Analytics**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/programming-for-business-analytics/MSIN0143).
- Term Two core modules: [**MSIN0097 Predictive Analytics**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/predictive-analytics/MSIN0097); [**MSIN0095 Operations Analytics**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/operations-analytics/MSIN0095).
- Term Two optional modules are chosen from an indicative list including [**MSIN0166 Data Engineering**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/data-engineering-MSIN0166), [**MSIN0167 Data Visualisation**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/data-visualisation-MSIN0167), [**MSIN0221 Natural Language Processing**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/natural-language-processing-MSIN0221), [**MSIN0088 Leading High-Performance Teams**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/leading-high-performance-teams-MSIN0088), [**MSIN0098 Technology Entrepreneurship**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/technology-entrepreneurship-MSIN0098), [**MSIN0148 Influence and Negotiations**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/influence-and-negotiations-MSIN0148), [**MSIN0159 Decision and Risk Analysis**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/decision-and-risk-analysis-MSIN0159), [**MSIN0226 Fintech**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/fintech-MSIN0226), [**MSIN0236 Managing Diversity**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/managing-diversity-MSIN0236), [**MSIN0261 Building Sustainable Ventures**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/building-sustainable-ventures-MSIN0261), and [**COMP0142 Machine Learning for Domain Specialists**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/machine-learning-for-domain-specialists-COMP0142). Optional modules are subject to change each year.
- Term Three: students undertake a [**Consulting/Dissertation Project**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/business-analytics-consulting-projectdissertation/MSIN0114). Students may undertake either a practical consulting project with organisations that have provided a challenging analytical project or an independent consulting/research project. Projects require application of skills learned in terms one and two and have historically resulted in a dissertation report of 12,000 words and a 15-minute presentation.
- Dissertation project types include Type One: Research Projects, Type Two: Technical Projects, and Type Three: Consultative Projects. The programme notes a more detailed overview of the [three types of dissertation projects](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/blog/exploring-innovation-three-types-dissertation-projects-our-business-analytics-programme).
- The majority of classes are taught at [Levels 38, 49, and 50 of One Canada Square, Canary Wharf](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/about/canary-wharf). Some optional modules will take place at the Bloomsbury campus.

- **Postgraduate student in UCL halls:** Rent range **£153-529 per week**; **£7,956-27,508 per 52 week academic year**. UCL postgraduate accommodation is usually offered on a 51 week contract.
- **Undergraduate or Postgraduate student in shared privately-rented accommodation:** Shared House - Rent range - excl. household bills: **£150-300 per week**, **£650-1300 per month**, **£7,800-15,600 per 52 week contract**.

Financial Aid.content:
- **MSc Business Analytics Scholarships:** A total of **£40,000** of scholarships are are available for outstanding candidates on the MSc Business Analytics programme. All applicants who apply to study MSc Business Analytics at UCL and who meet the scholarship criteria will be considered for scholarship funding.
- University College London offers a range of scholarships across all programmes. Postgraduate scholarships are typically awarded to the most talented students across a range of categories, and applicants wishing to obtain scholarships are strongly encouraged to apply early.
- **UCL East Scholarships:** This scholarship supports east Londoners by funding tuition fees and living costs of all UCL East Master’s programmes and select School of Management programmes. [Learn more about the UCL East Scholarship](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/ucl-east-london-scholarship)
- **UCL Global Master’s Scholarship:** The UCL Global Masters Scholarship aims to enable and encourage international students from lower income backgrounds to pursue full-time Master’s degree studies at UCL. There are **85 scholarships available each year worth up to £15,000 each**. The scholarship is awarded on the basis of financial need and upon the recommendation of the Student Funding Office. [Learn more about the UCL Global Master’s Scholarship](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/ucl-global-masters-scholarship)
- **UCL Musubi Global Master’s Scholarship (Japan):** There is **one scholarship of £20,250** available to a Japanese student applying to study during the **2026/2027 academic year**. [Learn more about the Musubi Global Master’s Scholarship](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/musubi-global-masters-scholarship)
- **UCL Fee Partnerships:** UCL has partnerships with external funding providers in which the university offers a contribution towards tuition fees. Applications for the awards listed should be made directly to the external funding body; applicants must also apply directly to UCL for a place on a programme of study at the same time. Applicants selected for the relevant external awards, who are also offered a place at UCL, will then automatically qualify for the fee contribution. [View the complete list of fee partnerships](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/fee-partnerships)
- **Fulbright Commission Award:** The Fulbright Commission Award is available for a US graduate student or those with equivalent experience in a relevant field to study any MSc programme at the UCL School of Management. Please note this is only available to citizens of the United States of America. [Learn more about the Fullbright Commission Award](https://fulbright.org.uk/our-programmes/fulbright-scholarships-to-the-uk/us-postgraduates/)
- UCL recommends using UCL’s [Scholarship Finder](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/scholarships-finder) to find all of the scholarships that are available. [Learn more about scholarships at UCL](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships)

Multiple Applications.content:
You may submit applications for a maximum of **two** taught graduate courses for entry to the 2026/27 academic year. The applications must be for different courses. Please note that if an application fee is charged, it will be charged per application. UCL does not accept multiple applications for the same course in the same academic year.
If you apply for more than one course the fee is payable for each application that requires an application fee.
Once you have submitted an application you cannot change the course that you have applied for. If you would like to apply for a different course, you will need to submit a new application for the course you wish to be considered for.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
UCL does not accept requests to defer, but will consider requests in exceptional circumstances outside the offer holder's control. Deferral requests are considered only for: serious illness of the offer holder or serious illness/death of a parent, guardian, partner or child; parental or adoption leave during the next 12 months; being directly and severely affected by a natural or human-made disaster; being awarded a UCL scholarship or full scholarship from a recognised funding body for study in the following academic year; or holding an offer to study the UCL International Pre-Masters.
To be eligible for a deferral, the offer holder must hold **an unconditional offer which has been accepted** and must have **paid the tuition fee deposit in full or be marked as exempt** if a deposit is required for the programme. If the request is approved, tuition fee deposit payments will be held on account until enrolment.
Deferral requests must be made on the offer page of the application portal. Requests due to illness or parental/adoption leave require a letter from a relevant medical practitioner. Scholarship-based requests require an official scholarship award letter. UCL reserves the right to request more information before making a final decision.
An application **cannot be deferred twice**. Applicants wanting to defer for two years must re-apply and be considered as a new application in competition with other applicants. The deadline for requesting a deferral is **two weeks prior to the start of the course**.
If the request is unsuccessful, applicants who cannot join that year may apply for the next academic year once applications open, but applications will be considered anew and in competition with all other applications for that intake. If a deferral is approved, a new offer letter will be issued and the applicant may need to take a new English test if the current English language qualification expires before the revised start date.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
You must meet all your conditions and hold an unconditional offer before you can enrol.
- Your offer letter will contain information on any deadlines that apply to your offer. If circumstances mean that you will not be able to meet your offer conditions by these dates, contact the [Graduate Admissions Team](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/stay-touch/ask-admissions-postgraduate-and-teacher-training-enquiries).
- Your offer letter will outline exactly which degree documents you need to provide. UCL cannot accept anything other than final official documents to meet the conditions of your offer.
- If you need to take an English language test to meet your offer conditions, UCL recommends booking a test as early as possible. If providing English language test scores, you must provide official results; UCL will not accept screenshots of your results portal.
- You can take a UCL Pre-sessional English course to settle the English language condition in your offer. See the [Pre-sessional English website](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/languages-international-education/preparation-courses/pre-sessional-english-courses/pg) for entry requirements, availability and applications.
- To clear offer conditions, upload copies to the applicant portal if you have an academic condition and have received your degree documents and transcripts from your university. Proof of English language proficiency must also be uploaded to the applicant portal.
- If you have not met your academic offer condition, you should still upload your documents; the Admissions team will still consider whether your offer can be confirmed.
- If you have not met your English language test condition but have received scores that meet the UCL level 1 requirement, you can still supply your test scores to UCL for review. UCL will not ordinarily accept a lower score than stipulated in the offer and cannot consider test scores that do not meet the UCL level 1 requirement.
